summary: A row of headline numbers, each on its own card (in Clean, a cell of one panel) with an icon, its change against the period before and a sparkline. A head holds a `title`, like Workspace, on the left and a period switch, such as 7 days, 30 days and Quarter, on the right; the switch rolls every number and line to the new values at once. It works as the top row of an agent dashboard, for numbers like runs, hours saved and spend.
use: At the top of a dashboard, to show the few numbers people check first.
When you want to show an agent's runs, time saved or cost at a glance.
When the same numbers need comparing across a few fixed periods.
features: Each card shows an icon, a label, a large number that rolls to its value, and its change against the period before as a percentage.

A sparkline per card draws in from the left, in the card's `color`, or the chart palette in order: the accent, then violet, green and orange. In Clean the four are cells of one panel, split by hairlines, with the title and period switch in an off-white head strip; each sparkline is a thin line in the same colours (the accent is white in Clean's dark mode), and the area under it fades from the line's colour to nothing.
Each stat has one entry in `values` per entry in `periods`, and switching the period updates every card together.
Pointing at the change shows the period's `compare` text, like "vs previous 30 days". The cards aren't buttons, so pointing at a card itself changes nothing.
`prefix` and `suffix` wrap the number, like "$" or "h".
`sparkRange` puts every sparkline on the same scale; by default each card scales to its own lowest and highest point.

The change sits in a tinted chip with dark text in its hue: green when the change is good news, red when it isn't, with a true minus sign. For a number that is better when it falls, like spend, set `lowerIsBetter` and a fall turns green.
Four across on a wide screen, and two by two on tablets and phones.
a11y: The period switch is a role="group" labelled "Period", with aria-pressed on the active option.
Screen readers hear the `compare` text after each number's change, so the comparison doesn't depend on pointing.
The sparkline draw-in is skipped, and number roll-ups finish at once, when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.a: No. The large number is rounded to a whole number and written with thousands separators, like 1,730. Pass a smaller unit, or put the unit in `suffix`, if you need finer detail.

faq.q: How do I compare sparklines across cards?
faq.a: Pass `sparkRange` as [bottom, top]. Every card then uses the same scale, so a taller line means a bigger value on every card.

faq.q: How do I hide the period switch?
faq.a: Pass a single entry in `periods`, with one value per stat. The switch only shows with two or more periods.
